enable: LD_PRELOAD this library and QUEST2_VIDC_BRIDGE=1 in the isolated donor process only
decode_owner: unchanged Quest OMX donor and real Venus backend
implemented: dynamic Venus H264 decoder discovery using sysfs, QUERYCAP and ENUM_FMT
seven exact private event subscriptions with process-owned queue and eventfd poll notification
real native SOURCE_CHANGE subscription, with unrepresentable payload explicitly rejected
actual backend EIO/ENODEV to subscribed SYS_ERROR, retaining original failure
flush completion only for known empty never-streaming queues
H264 standard control enum conversion retaining actual kernel capabilities and errno
standard DMABUF requests passed to real backend without data fabrication
operation fd/session pins, nonblocking decoder fd, real backend outside registry lock
poll eventfd duplication failures retained with cleanup rather than hidden timeouts
explicit QUEST2_VIDC_AUX_CAPS=1: real formatted auxiliary session REQBUFS and HFI minimum query for early EAGAIN
USERPTR_ION_to_DMABUF: one plane, zero allocation/data offset; actual fd/size and kernel attach checks
real buffer fd lifetime pins, backend returned slot count, donor 64-bit cookie restoration and actual dequeue metadata
QCOM EOS to native LAST and native LAST/ERROR to QCOM EOS/DATA_CORRUPT
not_implemented: USERPTR multiple planes or nonzero allocation/data offsets
private CODECCONFIG buffer flag without native equivalent
generic unmanaged-close concurrent dup2 transition: this is not a universal transparent fd layer
rules: Subscriptions may wait indefinitely for a condition that has not occurred; no fabricated completion events.
Unsupported private controls, queue formats and active flush operations fail EOPNOTSUPP.
MIN_BUFFERS_FOR_OUTPUT and CAPTURE return only values from the real driver; no guessed counts.
Auxiliary capability queries require paired kernel early-EAGAIN getters and no-STREAMON close SESSION_END fix; close success is not END confirmation, inspect kernel lifecycle evidence.
Managed close pins before its atomic descriptor/registry commit; EMFILE leaves original fd open and returns failure.
No device writes, firmware reset, provider reload, global service registration or filesystem node replacement.
